title: T-32 prices fix check: the host CREATES a pricing-manager plan through the game's own creation path (lever `pricesuggest make`, premise asserted); after a merge the client opens its partner copy of that plan the way the pricing screen does (lever `pricesuggest ask`: routed `recompute` to the runner), the host recomputes from its own shelves and its bundle carries the list back; the list the client's screen would show (lever `pricesuggest <id>` on the copy, where the local recompute is skipped) must EQUAL the host's: same count, same products and suggested prices (sugg= first 30, sig= fingerprint of the whole list). Ends dissolved, NO save
preconditions: Fixture save1 (host melaus, client Client1). Dev build on BOTH machines (the `pricesuggest` lever, src/DevT32.cs). The fixture has no pricing-manager plan (run T-PRICESUGGEST-20261113-150520 step 13: own=0 partnerRows=0), so step 5 creates one on the host BEFORE the merge, as a player would in BizMan > headquarters > Pricing Managers (PricingManagersPlanList.AddPlan :63-75, AssignEmployee :245, SetSupervisedNeighborhood PricingManagerPlanUI.cs:119). The fixture's host has NO employee with ba:skill_pricingmanager (run T-PRICESUGGEST-20261113-152356 step 5), so steps 5-7 get one the way a player does, BEFORE the plan: step 5 `pricesuggest recruit` runs the recruitment agency campaign's own candidate search (RecruitmentCampaign.CheckForCandidates :58-71 -> RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate, campaign shaped as RecruitmentAgencyDialog.cs:163-176 with business = the rented headquarters; find time now, no fee) and names a free pricing-manager workstation, the first open day and its opening hour - when every suitable workstation is already on a shift (run T-PRICESUGGEST-20261113-154513 step 5: suitable=10, all on a shift) it first frees ONE as a player does on the Schedule tab (ScheduleHelper.RemoveWorkShift :334-355, the shift slider's remove WorkShiftSlider.cs:208-211), removing the shift of an employee who has no ba:skill_pricingmanager and is on no plan, and names it as freed=employee@station/from-to; step 6 hires the candidate (`hire`, EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate, address = the headquarters); step 7 puts it on a shift through the Schedule tab (`shiftat`, ScheduleHelper.AddWorkShift as ScheduleEmployeeSelection.cs:60). FIXTURE REQUIREMENT: the host rents a headquarters with an open schedule day and a workstation suitable for ba:skill_pricingmanager that is free or held by a removable shift (an employee without ba:skill_pricingmanager, on no plan), the city has a recruitment agency, and the host runs at least one manageable (revenue, priced) business; if not, step 5 (or 8) answers ERR naming what is missing and the run stops there. The plan then reaches the client the way any host plan does (CompanyPlans partner rows, BuildPricing); both machines run the lever on the captured id.

steps.expect_result: ^OK pricesuggest recruit candidate=\S+ skill=\S+ day=[1-7] station=\S+ from=\d+ suitable=[1-9]\d* freed=\S+ .* hq=\S+ \S+$
steps.note: PREMISE: a ba:skill_pricingmanager candidate for the host's rented headquarters, produced by the recruitment campaign's own candidate search, and a free suitable workstation for it - freed=none when one was already free, else freed=employee@station/from-to names the ONE shift removed through ScheduleHelper.RemoveWorkShift (employee without ba:skill_pricingmanager, on no plan); ERR names a missing headquarters, agency, open day, or why no shift could be freed
PREMISE: the game's own hire (EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate); the candidate keeps the headquarters address the campaign gave it

steps.expect_result: ^OK pricesuggest shift st=${t32Station} emp=${t32Cand} day=${t32Day} .*shift=${t32From}-\d+ .*assigned=True addErr=none hq=
steps.note: PREMISE: the new pricing manager on a work shift at the headquarters, at DATA level with no screen (the Schedule-tab lever `shiftat` threw NullReference headless, run T-PRICESUGGEST-20261113-161858 step 7): what ScheduleHelper.AddWorkShift :292-327 does for a headquarters desk - a copy of the shift spanning the first opening slot on every open day by ScheduleDay.AddWorkShift, then the game's employee/HQ-plan update

PREMISE: the host creates its own plan (game's own creation path) BEFORE the merge, so only the host's own employees and shops are candidates; manager= is expected to be the employee hired at step 6 unless the save already had a free one; suggestions>=1 asserts the supervised shops have products
waits for the client's own settle line (searched from the previous step) instead of a fixed sleep

the HOST's own plan made at step 8, recomputed as the pricing screen does on open (PricingManagerPlanUI.LoadPlan:47); the result is read from the plan right after that recompute; copy=False: the runner computes

expect_log.regex: \[Merger\] plan edit applied for .*\(pricing recompute, plan ${t32Plan}, seq

steps.note: what opening the pricing screen on the client's copy does (PricingPlanCopies.AskRunner): the routed `recompute` reaches the host, which recomputes from its own shelves

expect_log.regex: \[PricingCopies\] plan ${t32Plan} of '${hostPid}': the runner's list is in \(n=\d+, sig=\S+,

steps.note: the host's urgent bundle after the recompute lands in the client's copy (CompanyPlans.Receive -> PricingPlanCopies.OnOwnerLists) with the host's count and fingerprint
the host's list as its routed recompute (step 18) left it - captured AFTER that recompute, so shelf or rival-price moves before step 18 cannot fail the gate (review F3)

steps.expect_result: ^OK pricesuggest agreement=${t32Plan} .* suggestions=${hostCount} sugg=${hostSugg} sig=${hostSig} copy=True own=

expect_log.regex: \[PricingCopies\] plan ${t32Plan}: a partner's copy - kept the runner's list

steps.note: PASS GATE: the list the client's screen shows for its copy (the local recompute is skipped, T-32 (a)) EQUALS the host's: count, first-30 products/prices and the whole-list fingerprint

steps.cmd: mark T32 PRICES REPORT plan=${t32Plan} nb=${madeNeighborhood} stores=${madeStores} host skill=${hostSkill} stores=${hostStores} n=${hostCount} sig=${hostSig} sugg=${hostSugg} | client skill=${clientSkill} stores=${clientStores} n=${clientCount} sig=${clientSig} sugg=${clientSugg}
steps.note: both machines' lists side by side in both logs (equality is asserted at step 21)
